summary: Ulster County, NY lookout: 65-ft tower taken over by the state in 1909, 73-ft replacement in 1930, staffing ended 1970, dismantled 1985.

facts.design: Steel lookout towers: 65 ft (1909), replaced by a 73 ft steel tower in 1930 with an observer's cabin
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 1985 after vandal damage; closed officially in 1984
facts.agency: New York State Forest, Fish and Game Commission (from 1909), later the Conservation Department

events.note: A 65-ft steel tower was established as a lookout station in May 1909, at a cost of $362.50; the state's Forest, Fish and Game Commission took the tower over that year; it had been used as an observation tower by a previous owner
Conservation commission announced an appointment for Belleayre Mountain, Charles Y. Parsons (spelled Persons elsewhere)
Frank Mead completed a new 73-ft steel tower and a new observer's cabin; sources disagree on whether it replaced a windmill tower or the original steel tower
State discontinued staffing of the observation tower
Belleayre Mountain Fire Tower officially closed
Damaged by vandalism, declared unsafe, and dismantled

corrections.proposed: New York State Forest, Fish and Game Commission (from 1909), later the Conservation Department
corrections.why: The current value is a date fragment from a source line, not an agency. The sources name the state commission that took over the lookout in 1909 and the Conservation Department in later years.
19.8 m (65 ft) is the height of the 1909 tower. The 73-ft steel tower built in 1930 is the later structure that both sources describe as the tower in service for decades.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1914 appointment notice spells the name Parsons; the 1949 and 1963 items and Bygone Hudson Valley spell it Persons. The story uses Persons, the spelling the other sources share.

Staffing ended in 1970 (Bygone Hudson Valley) and Catskill Country gives 1970 as the decommissioning year. Bygone Hudson Valley dates the official closure to 1984 and the dismantling to 1985, which matches the Forest Lookouts entry for 1985. The story gives each date with its source.

sources.title: Above the Clouds: When a Fire Tower Was Home

notes_for_editor: History is well documented from a local-history article and a transcribed clippings page, but no source describes what remains at the summit today, so access is omitted from facts. The brief's agency value ('May 1909:') and height (19.8 m, the 1909 tower) are corrected above. Unresolved: the 1930 report says the new tower replaced an old windmill tower, while Bygone Hudson Valley says it replaced the original steel tower. Walton Persons's tenure is 14 years in the 1949 item and 12 in the 1963 obituary. An FFLA New York group post titled 'Former fire tower site on Belleayre' appears in search results but could not be read from the cache, so it is not cited; it may describe the site today.
